title: Respect unsubscribe + email preferences across lifecycle sends and console surfaces
creator: Dylan Brooks
description:
Context
We’re ramping the Hosted API onboarding email drip v2 + adding in-console onboarding nudges during the 4-week lifecycle growth experiments sprint.

We need to ensure that ALL lifecycle email sends respect:
- CAN-SPAM unsubscribe requirements (global opt-out, no resubscribe without explicit action)
- GDPR requirements for preferences + suppression handling (honor opt-out quickly, keep minimal records to enforce suppression)
- Internal data-handling policy (audience exclusions; only approved event usage)

Current risk
- Email vendor suppression list is being applied inconsistently depending on send path (marketing-triggered vs product-triggered lifecycle sends).
- Console surfaces can generate “resend” actions that accidentally bypass suppression if implemented naively.
- We do not currently have a single source-of-truth preference state used by both trigger logic and UI.

Goal
Implement a single preference + suppression check that is enforced for any onboarding/lifecycle email send, and provide an in-console preferences management surface that is accurate, auditable, and compliant.

Scope
In scope:
- Preference state model + API (minimal)
- Unsubscribe & preferences link behavior in email templates (deep-link to console preferences page)
- Server-side suppression gate in lifecycle email trigger pipeline
- Console settings surface to view/update preferences
- Basic audit logging + metrics to prove compliance (suppressed sends, unsubscribe events)

Out of scope:
- Preference center for non-product marketing newsletters (owned by Marketing Ops)
- Full GDPR DSAR tooling (separate Security/Compliance initiative)

Acceptance criteria
1) Global opt-out: if a user unsubscribes, onboarding/lifecycle sends stop within 10 minutes (worst-case propagation).
2) Server-side enforcement: suppression is checked at send-time (not only at audience build time).
3) Console UX: user can view current state and update preferences; link is accessible from Console settings.
4) No bypass: any “resend onboarding email” or “send me this guide” actions must run through the same suppression gate.
5) Auditability: store minimal suppression record (user_id + timestamp + source) and emit events for:
   - email_unsubscribed
   - email_preferences_updated
   - lifecycle_email_send_suppressed
6) Compliance review sign-off captured in ticket comments (Michael Grant / Olga Petrov).

Implementation plan (engineering)
Backend
- Add preference record keyed by user_id with fields:
  - global_unsubscribed (boolean)
  - global_unsubscribed_at (timestamp)
  - updated_at, updated_by (system|user)
  - source (email_link|console|support)
- Create endpoint(s):
  - GET /v1/user/email-preferences (auth required)
  - POST /v1/user/email-preferences (auth required; supports global unsubscribe and limited category toggles if present)
- In lifecycle send pipeline:
  - Before enqueueing any email job, call PreferenceService.isSuppressed(user_id) and drop the send if true.
  - Emit lifecycle_email_send_suppressed with reason (global_unsubscribed|bounce_risk|complaint_risk if available).
- Webhook handling:
  - Ingest vendor unsubscribe events (SendGrid event webhook or equivalent) and set global_unsubscribed=true.
  - Deduplicate events by (user_id, event_type, day) to avoid flapping.

Console
- Add Settings -> Email preferences page:
  - Shows status (“You are unsubscribed from onboarding emails”)
  - CTA to resubscribe (explicit consent; sets global_unsubscribed=false)
  - Link target used by email footer: /settings/email-preferences?token=… (token optional; prefer authenticated)
- Ensure console “helpful actions” that send email (if any) call the lifecycle send endpoint that checks PreferenceService.

Telemetry
- Add events (names aligned with lifecycle event taxonomy):
  - lifecycle.email_unsubscribed
  - lifecycle.email_preferences_updated
  - lifecycle.email_send_suppressed
- Add counters in dashboards:
  - suppression_rate = suppressed / attempted
  - time_to_suppression (from unsubscribe click to first suppressed send)

Edge cases / decisions
- Resubscribe policy: allowed only via authenticated console action (no “one-click resubscribe” link in email).
- Data retention: keep suppression record indefinitely OR at least 24 months to ensure we don’t re-email an opted-out user after dormancy. (Confirm with Privacy.)
- If user deletes account: retain hashed email + suppression marker? (Out of scope for this sprint; track as follow-up.)

Testing
- Unit tests:
  - PreferenceService suppression logic
  - webhook ingestion and dedupe
- Integration tests:
  - lifecycle send endpoint refuses when suppressed
  - console updates reflect server state
- Manual QA:
  - unsubscribe from email -> verify no further onboarding emails (including triggered ones)
  - unsubscribe -> attempt console “resend” action (should be blocked/suppressed)

Rollout plan
- Ship behind feature flag: lifecycle_email_preferences_center
- Gradual enable:
  - Internal dogfood (Redwood employees)
  - 10% new signups cohort
  - 50% -> 100% if suppression events look correct and no support spike

Follow-ups (create separate tickets if not already)
- Add support tooling to force-unsubscribe for users who request via ticket (SUP workflow).
- Decide on account-deletion + suppression retention strategy (Privacy).
comments: 2026-01-17 (Dylan Brooks): Creating as P0 for sprint guardrails. We cannot scale lifecycle sends without server-side suppression gate + auditable preference state.

2026-01-18 (Tyler Benson): Marketing Ops: current SendGrid suppression list is reliable for marketing sends, but product-triggered sends need to consult the same state. Please avoid building audiences that “filter out unsubscribes” only at query time; we’ve seen race conditions.

2026-01-19 (Michael Grant): Legal (CAN-SPAM): Must include a clear unsubscribe mechanism in every lifecycle email. Global unsubscribe must be honored within 10 business days, but we should target same-day. Resubscribe should require affirmative action; do not re-enable via new signup events automatically.

2026-01-19 (Olga Petrov): GDPR: Keep preference record minimal, limit access via RBAC. Ensure user can view what they opted out of. If you store additional categories, treat as consent preferences and log changes.

2026-01-21 (Ethan Park): Plan: implement PreferenceService + send-time gate; console page will be in Settings with explicit resubscribe. Will wire vendor webhook -> preference update; add event emissions for suppression + updates.

2026-01-24 (Chloe Martin): Backend review: prefer storing user_id + email_hash for webhook mapping; some webhook events may arrive without our internal user_id. Also ensure suppression check is in the job worker as well (defense-in-depth).

2026-01-27 (Leila Farouk): QA note: include test for “unsubscribe then immediate send trigger” to validate propagation under 10 min; also verify link works when user is logged out (should prompt login, not error).
2026-01-30 (Ethan Park): Implemented + merged via PR-28505. Added console preferences page, API endpoints, and send-time suppression gate. Added new telemetry events and basic dashboard counters.

2026-02-06 (Allison Grant): Observability check: suppression_rate stable; no evidence of sends post-unsubscribe in the sampled cohort. Marking Done; follow-up needed for account deletion retention policy.
